title: Architecture & Standards — API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance (ADRs)
author: Avery Chen
short_intro: This page consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards for public APIs, code style, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also summarizes active/important ADRs that affect these areas. The goal is to provide a single, opinionated reference for engineers designing services and model-serving pipelines that must meet our production economics, reliability, and security requirements.
scope: Applies to all backend services, model-serving components (hosted, dedicated, private), and infra owned by Redwood Inference. Client SDKs should follow the API standards section unless a language-specific exception is documented.
principles:
- Production-first: every design must surface SLO, cost, and operational considerations up-front.
- Observable-by-default: instrument for traces, metrics, and structured logs at service boundaries.
- Backwards-compatible: API changes should be backwards compatible or follow the documented deprecation process.
- Secure-by-design: default secure configurations (TLS, RBAC, least privilege) for all deployments.
- Reproducible infra: use IaC and immutable artifacts for deployments.
owners:
- Standards owner: Eng Architecture (eng-platform)
- Primary reviewers: API Platform, Serving Runtime, Eng SRE
- Escalation: Head of Eng Architecture
api_standards:
Overview
- Public HTTP APIs should be RESTful and JSON over HTTPS unless otherwise justified (e.g., streaming gRPC for high-throughput ML traffic).
- All new APIs must include an OpenAPI (v3) spec checked into the service repository under /api/openapi.yaml.
- Versioning: use semantic path versioning (/v1/...), not content negotiation. Deprecation windows must be documented and communicated (minimum 90 days for public customers).

Authentication & Authorization
- Production APIs must support OAuth2 bearer tokens and mutual TLS for private deployments where required.
- Token scopes should be narrow and documented in the OpenAPI spec.

Error handling
- Use standard HTTP status codes. Prefer 4xx for client errors and 5xx for server errors.
- Error responses must be JSON with fields: code, message, request_id, and optionally details.

Rate limiting & Quotas
- All public endpoints must integrate with API gateway rate limiting. Default quota enforcement: 100 req/s for free-tier endpoints; configurable per-customer for Dedicated plans.
coding_standards:
- Languages and formatters: follow the repo-level language style (gofmt/clang-format/black/ruff etc). Prefer idiomatic language usage over micro-style rules.
- Static analysis: all services must run linters and type-checking in CI (gosec, clang-tidy, bandit, mypy where applicable).
- Tests: unit tests, component tests for critical paths, and a smoke test that runs in CI for every merge to main. Coverage thresholds are advisory (>= 60% for core infra services).
- Dependency management: pin transitive dependencies and use Dependabot or equivalent. Security-critical libraries must be reviewed by SecOps before upgrade.
infra_standards:
- IaC: Terraform for cloud infra, Helm/Kustomize for k8s manifests. Store state in centrally-managed backend (Terraform Cloud or S3 with locking).
- Environments: dev, staging, prod. Staging must be production-like for critical infra (same instance types, similar scale profile for serving tests).
- Secrets: no plaintext secrets in repos. Use KMS-backed secret stores (AWS KMS + SSM Parameter Store / HashiCorp Vault for Private deployments).
- Networking: services must segment traffic by function and use private subnets for model-serving workers. All control-plane communication must be authenticated and logged.
model_serving_standards:
- Model catalog & manifests: Every model served must have a model manifest (YAML) with identifiers: model_name, version, architecture, quantization_profile, preferred_kernels, and evaluation_report_id.
- Runtime behavior: Support model variants: natively-loadable float32, int8-quantized, and a CPU-fallback where feasible. KV-cache semantics and eviction policies must be explicit in model manifests (default LRU, max_cache_size per-host).
- Operational controls: Per-model SLOs and per-route routing policies must be configurable in the control plane. Canary and rollout policy: default canary = 1% traffic for 24 hours with automated health checks (latency, error-rate, quality regressions on a curated eval set).
observability_standards:
- Metrics: All services must export Prometheus-compatible metrics. Metric names must use the kebab_case prefix app/service_<name>_. Standard metrics: request_count, request_latency_seconds_bucket (summary/histogram), error_count, queue_depth, gpu_utilization (for serving hosts).
- Tracing: Distributed tracing via OpenTelemetry. Span names should include service.operation and resource identifiers (model_id, request_id). Sampling: dynamic sampling at gateway; default sample_rate = 0.01 for high-traffic paths, 1.0 for error traces.
- Logging: Structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, level, service, env, request_id, trace_id, tenant_id (when applicable), message, and details.
- Alerts & Dashboards: SRE will maintain per-service dashboards and on-call runbooks. Alert thresholds must map to SLO burn rate policies (see SLO table below).
performance_standards:
SLOs and thresholds (examples)
| component | SLO (p95) | Error budget (monthly) | Alert threshold |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| API gateway (public gen) | 300 ms | 0.5% | p95 > 400 ms for 5m |
| Model-serving tail latency | 2.0 s (inference p95) | 1.0% | p95 > 2.5 s for 10m |
| Embeddings endpoint (small models) | 120 ms | 0.5% | p95 > 180 ms for 5m |

Performance guidance
- Batching: use adaptive batching for GPU-backed models with target latency budgets configurable per-model.
- Quantization profiles: prefer int8 where offline eval shows <1% quality delta on business-critical eval sets.
- Autoscaling: prefer proactive scaling based on predicted load + reactive pod/instance autoscaling by CPU/GPU queue depth.
adrs_and_decisions:
Summary of active ADRs (high level)
1) ADR-2026-01: Standardize External API Versioning
- Decision: path-based semantic versioning (/v1/...).
- Rationale: simpler client caching and gateway routing; explicit deprecation.
- Consequences: must support simultaneous versions for a minimum deprecation window.
- Status: accepted (2026-01-08) — owners: Priya Kapoor (API Platform)

2) ADR-2026-03: Default Inference Runtime Kernel Selection
- Decision: use runtime kernel selector that prefers vendor-provided optimized kernels (cuBLAS/cuDNN equivalents) with fallback to Triton-compatible kernels. Kernel selection is recorded per-request in trace metadata.
- Rationale: maximize throughput and reduce memory overhead while maintaining deterministic fallbacks for limited hardware.
- Consequences: added complexity in regression testing for kernels; requires expanded benchmarking matrix in CI.
- Status: accepted (2026-02-15) — owners: Diego Morales (Serving Runtime)

3) ADR-2025-11: Observability Baseline
- Decision: adopt OpenTelemetry for traces and Prometheus for metrics; enforce structured logs.
- Status: accepted (2025-11-20) — owners: Lena Fischer (Eng SRE)
runbooks_and_playbooks:
- API change rollout checklist
  1. Add OpenAPI spec and contract tests in PR.
  2. Create migration plan and deprecation notice (90 days) for public APIs.
  3. Deploy to staging and run contract/compatibility tests.
  4. Canary deploy to production (1% traffic, 24h) and monitor SLOs, error rates, and eval set quality.
  5. If stable, increase rollout to 10% then 100% following standard escalation windows.

- Incident triage (high-level)
  1. Pager triggers on SLO burn/alert.
  2. Triage owner acknowledges and collects: service, region, last deploy, error-rate, SLO dashboards, recent changes.
  3. Rollback or route-around if rollbackable; otherwise follow mitigation steps in service runbook.
testing_and_ci_requirements:
- All services must pass unit tests + linting before merge.
- Integration tests that exercise model-serving must run nightly and on tag builds for release candidates.
- Benchmark suite: runtime and kernel benchmarks run in a dedicated perf CI lane; regressions >5% must be triaged before release.
security_and_compliance_notes:
- Data residency: ensure model-serving in Private deployments respects region-specific data residency settings. See related pages for the customer requirements library.
- Audit logging: control plane must log model loads, rollouts, and access to model artifacts.
